activities.title: Model a complete debugging task
activities.purpose: Show a synthetic debugging task from symptom through hypothesis, trace, correction and verification.
activities.guidance: Use one connected whole-task example. Explain non-routine reasoning separately from just-in-time routine tracing instructions. Observing a solution is not evidence of independent performance.

mappings.rationale: A fully supported model of the whole debugging task; use before less-supported performance.
Make hypothesis selection and verification reasoning available before and during the non-routine task aspects.
Present routine variable-tracing steps just when the learner needs them; fade support with evidence.

activities.title: Recognize a routine trace result
activities.purpose: Practice identifying a variable value in a short synthetic trace tied to the current debugging task.
activities.guidance: Use part-task practice only for a routine skill explicitly requiring automaticity, after introducing it in a meaningful whole task. Return to the whole task afterward. Recognition practice cannot certify independent debugging competency.

mappings.rationale: Eligible only when the focus skill is routine, requires automaticity and needs additional practice beyond whole tasks.

activities.title: Explain and repair a synthetic defect
activities.purpose: Ask for a diagnosis, correction and verification explanation for one connected synthetic programming task.
activities.guidance: Request reasoning and verification, not only a final answer. Adapt support to evidence. Keep the response pending authorized instructor review; do not execute submitted code or infer formal competency from part-task success.

mappings.rationale: Integrate routine tracing and non-routine diagnosis in a whole debugging task; require instructor review before authoritative scoring.
